clue.text: Rambler has just one shoe

definitions.meaning: a rambling climbing plant that creeps over walls and fences
brothel ... are thick-soled suede shoes, so a single one of the pair

explanation.surface: A hiker sets out wearing only a single shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambler' suggests a walker, which fits the shoe picture, but it is the plant. Creepers are crepe-soled shoes, sold as a pair, hence 'just one'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler is a climbing plant, and a single brothel-creeper shoe is also named by this word.

clue.text: Its points are named by boxers

definitions.text: Its points are named by boxers

parts.words: Its points are named by boxers
parts.note: to box the instrument is to recite its thirty-two directions in order, so the boxers are sailors reciting, not fighters scoring points

explanation.surface: Prizefighters score points that the judges announce.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxers and points suggest a boxing match; in sailing, 'boxing' the instrument means naming all its directions in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors learn to box this navigational instrument by naming its thirty-two points in sequence.

clue.text: Bird decapitated dog

indicators.note: with its head cut off, so the first letter of the dog breed goes

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of hunting dog

explanation.surface: A bird kills a dog by tearing its head off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decapitated' removes the B of BEAGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bird of prey, an example of the category bird.

clue.text: Birds are quiet, having no right being in groups of fruit trees

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction for soft

indicators.note: lacking it, so the named letter is taken out of the orchards

parts.note: orchards are plantings of fruit trees

explanation.surface: Birds keep silent in the orchards when nobody has permission to be there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no' removes the first R from the orchards, leaving OCHARDS. 'Birds are' joins definition to wordplay; 'being in' links the fruit trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Pochards are diving ducks, examples of birds.

clue.text: Lay down the line to be followed

definitions.meaning: a regulation or principle that must be kept to

explanation.definitionFit: To lay down the law is to decree; a principle everyone must follow is a regulation of the same name.

clue.text: Changes of menu are good for a girl

indicators.note: the letters of the next words are changed around into a new order

explanation.surface: Altering the restaurant's menu is good news for one young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes of' rearranges MENU ARE; 'are good for' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional female first name, so an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: But will the hawthorn flower?

parts.note: the question asks whether the shrub might bloom; split differently, the shrub's flower is named after a spring month plus bloom

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders whether the hawthorn will bloom this year.
explanation.walkthrough: Hawthorn flowers in spring are named after the month they appear; the doubtful question reads as 'may blossom'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawthorn blooms in late spring and its white flowers are traditionally called by the month they open.

clue.text: University student drop-out turned up the previous month

parts.note: L is a learner driver, a crossword student

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to drop out something is to omit it

explanation.surface: A university student who quit college last month returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses the word for drop out, making TIMO. In old business letters this Latin word meant last month, as in 'your letter of the 5th ultimo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Old commercial correspondence used this Latin term for last month, as in 'your letter of the 5th'.

clue.text: Branded stock

parts.note: livestock marked as belonging to an owner by a cut or tag on the ear; also anything set aside for a purpose

explanation.definitionFit: Farm animals were identified by a notch on the ear, so marked livestock were said to be so; figuratively, reserved for a purpose.

clue.text: Physician upset, in din injurious to health

indicators.note: the reversed doctor sits inside the word for din

parts.note: a din is a loud noise

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor is upset that the racket is damaging people's health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the doctor's letters into OM, and 'in' places them inside the din. The comma hides the break between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Noxious or harmful, especially of a smell, the sense of being unwholesome.

clue.text: Employing hocus-pocus, wise men about to join forces

parts.note: the Magi were the wise men of the Nativity
C is circa, Latin for about
to ally is to unite with another

explanation.surface: Three wise men practise conjuring tricks before forming an alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: Hocus-pocus is conjuring or trickery, so employing it means doing things by sorcery.

clue.text: Planter, ailing, requires a sunhat

indicators.note: the opening words need, or contain, the answer within them

explanation.surface: A sick colonial planter needs a hat against the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in plan(TER AI)ling. A colonial planter would wear one, which helps the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed felt hat with a double crown, worn in hot climates against the sun.

clue.text: Primate on English isle a Neanderthal type?

parts.note: an ape is a primate
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea, is a Crown dependency off England

explanation.surface: A monkey on an island off England resembles a caveman.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is not part of England, so 'English isle' is loose but fair; 'on' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A primitive human or hominid, the popular image of an early cave-dwelling ancestor.

clue.text: Parking a pain in this plant!

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
lumbago is pain in the lower back

explanation.surface: Parking is a nuisance near this particular plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a pain' seems to be a complaint about parking; it is a specific back pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus of plants also called leadwort, with blue flowers.

clue.text: Around the circle,everyone can sew badly, making these excuses

indicators.note: everyone stands round about, next to, the circle, so the circle comes straight after

parts.note: all means every person
a circle is shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: the letters of the words are badly arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Everyone sitting round in a sewing circle makes excuses for poor stitching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges CAN SEW into WANCES. 'Around' says everyone is gathered beside the circle, and 'making these' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Making allowances for someone means pardoning or excusing their shortcomings.

clue.text: Run one's eyes over unusually developed ladies and cause offence

parts.note: to scan is to look over quickly

indicators.note: developed in an unusual way, the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A leering man stares at women's figures and offends them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually developed' rearranges the ladies into DALISE. The surface of ogling is a red herring for looking quickly over a page.
explanation.definitionFit: To shock or outrage people's sense of propriety, giving offence.

clue.text: Point to a weapon in a war Herod abandoned

indicators.note: wild and unrestrained, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A biblical king gives up a war and points to a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' suggests Herod quitting the war, but it rearranges A WAR HEROD.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed tip fixed on the front of an arrow shaft, the business end of the missile.

clue.text: Risky enterprise involves this part of Scotland

indicators.note: the words take in, or contain, the answer across the word break

explanation.surface: A dangerous venture is taking place in a Scottish region.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in ri(SKY E)nterprise.
explanation.definitionFit: An island of the Inner Hebrides off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Girl decorating some cakes

definitions.meaning: the candied green stalks of a herb used as cake decoration

explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, and also a herb whose crystallised stems decorate cakes and trifles.

clue.text: Hurt of love rejected

indicators.note: thrown back, so the word for love is read backwards

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: A jilted lover is pained by rejection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses EROS.
explanation.definitionFit: Painful or aching, as a bruised limb is tender.

clue.text: Record performance in Wimbledon match?

definitions.meaning: a tennis player behind by one set has had this result

explanation.definitionFit: To set down is to write down; a tennis player trailing by a set in a match is one set behind.

clue.text: Odd end, as internal piping leads to lines of pillars

parts.note: the colon is a tube of the large intestine, and it leads, coming first, ahead of the rearranged letters

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters are arranged into a strange order

explanation.surface: A strange tube full of internal pipes ends in rows of columns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' looks like an adjective for 'end' but rearranges END AS into NADES; 'leads to' says the gut tube comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonnade is a row of columns supporting a roof, so plural rows of columns.

clue.text: Shoots sitting ducks?

definitions.meaning: new growths from a plant's root or stem
easy targets or dupes, people easily fooled

explanation.definitionFit: Shoots springing from roots of a plant share the name with gullible victims easily taken in.

clue.text: Makes experimental attempts to produce literary work

explanation.definitionFit: To attempt something is an old sense of the verb; short prose compositions share the spelling.

clue.text: Douglas chap, perhaps, seen to drag two poles to his island home?

parts.note: to tow is to drag along
N, the north pole
S, the south pole
the Isle of Man, whose capital is Douglas

explanation.surface: A man from Douglas hauls a pair of poles back home to his island.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man, a town, so its inhabitant fits the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A town dweller, and a man of Douglas lives in a town.

clue.text: Fellow caught one short of a century, agitated

parts.note: he refers to a male, a fellow
ct is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
IC is ninety-nine in Roman numerals, one less than C

explanation.surface: A batsman caught on ninety-nine is in a frantic state.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a century is a hundred runs, and IC is a loose Roman numeral for 99.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic and busy, marked by excited, agitated activity.

clue.text: There's a lot in gin for the traveller

indicators.note: the letter for a lot goes inside the word for gin

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap
M, a thousand, a large number

explanation.surface: A heavy-drinking traveller has plenty of gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' is not the drink but a snare, TRAP, with M (a thousand) inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagrant who walks from place to place, a wanderer of the road.

clue.text: Intimate the artillery's heading north

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: guns are artillery

explanation.surface: Intimating that the artillery is moving north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading north' reverses GUNS. 'Intimate' is the adjective, cosy, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosy and private, the sense of close and comfortable.

clue.text: Show ring to which a salesman returns

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

indicators.note: comes back, so the run is read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman returns to the boxing ring for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses A REP to PERA after O.
explanation.definitionFit: A staged dramatic musical work, an example of a show.

clue.text: Frank had a meal with applicant

parts.note: frank means candid, open
ate is the past of eat

explanation.surface: An honest interviewee lunched with a job applicant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name but means open and honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone seeking a job or office is a contender put forward.

clue.text: Bearskins, it's said they favour?

parts.note: the guards' fur hats sound like uncovered skin, which some people prefer to wear and nothing else

explanation.surface: Guardsmen are said to prefer their tall fur hats.
explanation.walkthrough: Bearskins are the tall fur caps of British guardsmen; spoken, the word sounds like 'bare skins'.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturists prefer going unclothed, showing uncovered skin.

clue.text: Whale of a weight, Manx cat carried

parts.note: a gram is a unit of weight

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word for cat loses its last letter

parts.note: puss is a cat

explanation.surface: A whale of a weight carried a tailless cat from the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: Manx cats, from the Isle of Man, are tailless, so PUSS loses its tail, S.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for the killer whale or Risso's dolphin, a small toothed whale.
